memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"'...I will bring on you sudden terror, wasting diseases and fever that
will destroy your sight and drain away your life. You will plant seed in
vain, because your enemies will eat it. I will set my face against you so
that you will be defeated by your enemies'" - Lev 26:16b-17a (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
These are hard words describing the consequences of covenant-breaking for
Israel: sickness, fear, wasted labour, defeat. We must handle such
passages honestly rather than rushing past them.

The heaviest phrase is planting seed in vain. There is a particular
anguish in labouring hard and seeing nothing come of it — sowing, and
another eating the harvest. It is the picture of a life stripped of
fruitfulness.

Let us be clear and pastoral. This described the specific covenant
consequences for the nation of Israel. It is not a template for reading
every believer's hardship. When your labour feels fruitless or illness
comes, it does not mean God has set His face against you. The New Covenant
believer is never under God's condemnation (Rom 8:1).

But the passage does teach us something true: a life pulled away from God
tends towards emptiness. Sin promises fullness and delivers famine. The
prodigal son found this in a distant country, feeding pigs and longing for
their food (Luke 15:14-16).

Dear friend, if your life feels strangely fruitless — if you are working
hard and something still feels empty — do not ignore it. Rather than
reading it automatically as punishment, ask God to search your heart and
show you whether you have drifted from the source of true life.

Jesus said, apart from me you can do nothing (John 15:5). Fruitfulness
flows from nearness to Him. Return to the vine.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Does any part of my life feel strangely empty or fruitless?
2. Have I drifted from Christ, the source of true fruitfulness?
3. What would returning to Him look like for me today?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Father, search my heart. Where I have drifted from You into emptiness,
draw me back to Christ, the true vine, that my life may bear fruit again.
Amen.
